title: Boundary-lifting maps of quasicategories are coherent equivalences
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, equivalence edges and coherent functor equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $p:X\to Y$ be a simplicial map between quasicategories. Suppose that for every $n\geq0$ every commutative square with left map $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ and right map $p$ admits a diagonal filler, where $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of the proper faces and $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Then there exist a simplicial map $s:Y\to X$ and a coherent natural equivalence $\eta:\mathrm{id}_X\simeq sp$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(X,X)$ such that $ps=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $p\eta$ is the degenerate transformation of $p$. In particular the specified map $p$ is a coherent functor equivalence. This includes empty quasicategories; no Kan condition on $X$ or $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08NS, label lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy (section and cylinder homotopy), using Tag 08NM, label lemma-trivial-kan. The coherent-equivalence assertion is an agent expansion for quasicategories, not an assertion of the Stacks lemma; pointwise equivalences are as in lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus.

proof.text: The stated boundary lifting condition is exactly that p is a trivial Kan fibration in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], including the n=0 condition because the degree-zero boundary is empty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to the degreewise injection ∅→Y, with the unique map ∅→X and id_Y. This gives a simplicial map s:Y→X with p s=id_Y.

source.place: Tag 08NM, label lemma-trivial-kan, applied to the degreewise injection of the empty simplicial set into Y; Definition 08NL, label definition-trivial-kan, for surjectivity from the n=0 boundary.

proof.text: Let j:∂Δ[1]×X→Δ[1]×X be the endpoint inclusion. Define a on the two endpoint copies to be id_X at 0 and s p at 1, and define b=p∘pr_X. Since p s=id_Y, the two endpoint restrictions satisfy p a=b j. The map j is degreewise injective, so [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] gives H:Δ[1]×X→X with H|_0=id_X, H|_1=s p, and p H=p pr_X. Thus H is an interval transformation over p.

source.place: Tag 08NS, label lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy, endpoint-cylinder lifting square, reconstructed with the stated lifting lemma

proof.text: For a vertex x of X, the track H_x:Δ[1]→X has endpoints x and s(p x), and p H_x is the degenerate edge at p x by p H=p pr_X. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to ∂Δ[1]→Δ[1] with endpoint values s(p x),x and degenerate base edge; this supplies an edge inverse to H_x. Apply the same lifting statement to the two boundary inclusions ∂Δ[2]→Δ[2] whose boundaries are (H_x,H_x^{-1},id_x) and (H_x^{-1},H_x,id_{s(p x)}), with degenerate base 2-simplices. The resulting 2-simplices witness both inverse equations. By the definition of equivalence edge in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], every H_x is an equivalence.

source.place: Tag 08NM boundary lifting, combined with the equivalence-edge definition in the enhanced simplicial conventions

proof.text: By the internal-functor construction in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], H represents an edge from id_X to s p in Fun(X,X). The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that this edge is an equivalence because every vertex component H_x is an equivalence. Hence η:=H is a coherent natural equivalence id_X≃s p. The identity p H=p pr_X says that pη is the degenerate transformation of p, while Step 1 gives p s=id_Y. These are exactly the asserted section and coherent inverse data, so p is a coherent functor equivalence.
